title: Rejecting an Out-of-Range Recorded Step
statement: Let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine on Boolean symbols with state set $Q$, let $T$ be a tag set, let $u:T\times\{\text{blank},0,1\}\to T$ be a tag update rule, and let $S$ be the state set of a two-work-tape seeking machine with designated states $s_0,s_1$. Let $d$ be a four-work-tape configuration over the record alphabet, let $w$ be a finite record word, and let $D$ be recorded step data for $M$. If the data indicate that the simulated step moves a work-tape head outward from a recorded boundary, then the record-processing machine has a run of exactly $2|w|+3$ steps from the snapshot with control given by applying the recorded step to $D$, unshifted heads, and a buffer containing $w$ on the first buffer tape, to the snapshot with rejecting verdict control, unshifted heads, and empty buffers. Before the final step it visits neither verdict state, and every work-tape head remains within distance $|w|+1$ of its initial position.
hypotheses_covered: M is a k-work-tape Boolean Turing machine
u is a tag update rule
seek is a two-work-tape machine with designated start and finish states
d is a four-work-tape record-alphabet configuration
w is a finite record word
data D are recorded step data for M
the out-of-range test for M and D is true
caveat: The out-of-range predicate and snapshot notation are private constructions; the prose describes the predicate as an outward move from a recorded boundary.
